question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose a top-level `auth` namespace alongside the established `models auth` namespace for model-auth profile inspection?
rationale: The shortcut is technically feasible but creates a new documented public CLI contract and conflicts with the repository preference for one canonical path; code review cannot choose that product taxonomy safely.

options.title: Keep models auth canonical
options.body: Decline the alias and retain `openclaw models auth list` as the only supported model-auth listing path.

options.title: Approve the top-level alias
options.body: Accept the permanent compatibility surface, refactor both paths through one shared registrar, and require live command proof before merge.

options.title: Design a broader auth namespace
options.body: Pause this narrow alias until maintainers define whether top-level `auth` should own additional provider, channel, or operator-auth commands consistently.

recommendation.title: Keep models auth canonical
recommendation.body: Decline the alias and retain `openclaw models auth list` as the only supported model-auth listing path.

likelyOwner.reason: The current canonical model-auth listing and adjacent auth/CLI ownership history most strongly route this taxonomy decision here.
